notes: Lake shape holds, but the paint is a soft pastel wash. Does not have Monet's broken light on water.
Island church dissolves into the shore. Water is brushed, but the landmark that makes the place is weakened.
Canal and facades stay readable. Windows go muddy; looks filtered more than painted.
Mountain outline is kept. Colour is pretty, not really Monet — too even, too little flicker in the light.
Cliff line survives. Sky has banding and a repeated stroke pattern that looks generated.
Bridge is there, but lilies and water look pasted and flat. Still halfway a painting.
Sunset sky takes loose colour well. Surf edge is smeared.
Buildings and bridge read as a real canal photo. A little grain, nothing broken.
Rotunda and columns are too sharp for Monet. Content is excellent; style is only a tint.
Garden is photographic enough. Flower beds clump and lose individual blooms.
Facade looks photographed. Some carved detail is smoothed, but brushwork is gone.
Boats look real. Water has a plastic sheen.
International-orange bridge goes dull and cables smear. Iconic structure is damaged, style is muddy.
Pond layout kept, result still looks like a soft painting, not a photo.
Outdoor light is photographic. Face and hands are simplified; dress folds vanish.
Red boat and quay stay put. Strokes are visible, boat is still a bit hard-edged.
Parliament could pass as a travel photo. Windows and reflection hold.
Masts and hulls held. Water still carries brush marks.
Bridge and willows survive the conversion. Water is soft but believable.
Matterhorn is unmistakable. Strokes sit on top of a photo; light on the snow is not broken up.
Water reflections take colour patches. Palace edges fray; sky is thin.
Cranes can be named, but booms and rigging turn to noise. Texture looks sprayed on.
People on the beach become blobs. Faces and limbs are not there. Unusable.
Harbour looks shot on a camera. Small boats shift a little.
Flower field takes broken colour. Peaks are slightly melted at the ridge.
Footbridge and path look like a garden photograph. Foliage is only mildly soft.
Lily pads blur into the pond. Flower groups move. Not a clean photo.
Path and border plantings read as a real garden. Colour is cooler than the painting.
Haystack stays, sky is wiped out and flat. Contrast collapse is obvious.
Domes and sea barely change. This is a texture overlay, not a Monet translation.
